species.name: Human
species.description:
3.1 Human
Humans are the baseline of the Imperium: adaptable, 
ambitious, fragile, and dangerously determined.
Ability Scores: +2 to one ability score and +1 to 
another.
Size: Medium.
Speed: 30 ft.
Available Classes: Veteran, Zealot, Psyker, Arbites 
Enforcer, Hive Scum.
3.1.1 Human Traits
Imperial Adaptability: Gain proficiency in one skill of 
your choice.
Broad Training: Gain one additional weapon, tool, or 
language proficiency.
Faith, Fear, or Discipline: Once per long rest, when you 
fail a saving throw, you may reroll it. You must
use the new result.

species.name: Ratling Abhuman
species.description:
3.3 Ratling Abhuman
Ratlings are small abhumans known for stealth, 
marksmanship, scavenging, cooking, black-market
dealings, and improbable survival.
Ability Scores: +2 Dexterity, +1 Wisdom.
Size: Small.
Speed: 25 ft.
Available Classes: Ratling Sharpshooter, Veteran, Hive 
Scum.
3.3.1 Ratling Traits
Darkvision: You have darkvision to a range of 60 ft (see 
the rules at the start of this chapter).
Small Target: When you have light cover, you may treat 
it as heavy cover.
Sniper’s Eye: You ignore disadvantage from attacking at 
long range with weapons that have the
Accurate property.
Naturally Sneaky: You gain proficiency in Stealth.
Lucky Shot: Once per short rest, when you miss with a 
ranged weapon attack, you may reroll the
attack.
Bad in a Straight Fight: You have disadvantage on 
Strength checks made to shove or grapple creatures
larger than you.

species.name: Ogryn Abhuman
species.description:
3.2 Ogryn Abhuman
Ogryns are massive abhumans used by the Imperium as 
shock troops, bodyguards, line-breakers, and
living siege weapons. They are loyal and terrifyingly 
durable, but they are not subtle and struggle with
equipment designed for normal human frames.
Ability Scores: +2 Strength, +1 Constitution.
Size: Medium, but you count as one size larger for 
carrying, lifting, pushing, dragging, grappling, and
shoving.
Speed: 30 ft.
Available Classes: Ogryn Skullbreaker only.
3.2.1 Ogryn Traits
Massive Build: Your maximum hit points increase by 3 
per character level. You also count as one size
larger for carrying, lifting, pushing, dragging, grappling, 
and shoving.
Thick Skull: You have advantage on saving throws 
against being frightened.
Brute Strength: Your unarmed strikes deal 1d6 + your 
Strength modifier bludgeoning damage.
Too Big for Standard Kit: You cannot use most 
standard armour, delicate weapons, compact firearms,
or subtle tools unless they have been modified for Ogryn 
use.
Simple Solutions: You are not automatically stupid, but 
you struggle with delicate logic, subtle
interfaces, encrypted systems, and advanced technology. 
You have disadvantage on Intelligence checks
involving advanced technology, forbidden lore, cogitators, 
security systems, encrypted data, or complex
machinery unless you are proficient in a relevant skill or 
tool. However, once per short rest, when a
problem could plausibly be solved through brute force, 
intimidation, endurance, or direct action, you
may add your proficiency bonus to the check even if you 
would not normally be proficient.

species.name: Skitarii Augmented Human
species.description:
3.4 Skitarii Augmented Human
Skitarii are cybernetically enhanced soldiers of the 
Adeptus Mechanicus. They are machine-disciplined,
sensor-linked, and doctrinally conditioned beyond normal 
human limits.
Ability Scores: +2 Dexterity or Intelligence, +1 
Constitution.
Size: Medium.
Speed: 30 ft.
Available Classes: Skitarii Veteran.
3.4.1 Skitarii Traits
Augmetic Body: You have resistance to poison damage 
and advantage on saving throws against
disease.
Machine Discipline: You have advantage on saving 
throws against being charmed.
Noospheric Focus: Gain proficiency in Investigation, 
Perception, or Technology.
Integrated Auspex: Once per short rest, as a bonus 
action, choose one creature within 60 ft that you
can see. Your next attack against that creature before 
the end of your turn gains +1d4 to hit.
Cybernetic Maintenance: During a short rest, if you or 
an ally has tinker’s tools or Mechanicus tools,
you may regain additional hit points equal to your 
proficiency bonus.
No Psychic Potential: You cannot choose the Psyker 
class or any trait that grants psychic powers.

species.name: Squat / Kin
species.description:
3.5 Squat / Kin
Squats, often known as Kin in modern Imperial records, 
are hardy void-adapted abhumans associated
with holds, guilds, oath-bands, mining fleets, mercenary 
contracts, and ancient grudges. They are
shorter than humans but dense, resilient, technically 
minded, and extremely difficult to intimidate.
Ability Scores: +2 Constitution, +1 Intelligence or 
Wisdom.
Size: Medium, but your height is usually between 4 and 5 
ft.
Speed: 25 ft.
Available Classes: Kin Armsman, Hernkyn Prospector.
3.5.1 Squat / Kin Traits
Darkvision: You have darkvision to a range of 60 ft (see 
the rules at the start of this chapter).
Dense Build: You have advantage on saving throws 
against being shoved, knocked prone, or moved
against your will.
Void-Hardened: You have advantage on saving throws 
against exhaustion caused by poor atmosphere,
bad rations, forced marches, cramped voidship 
conditions, mining hazards, or environmental hardship.
Guild-Craft: Gain proficiency in Technology, 
Investigation, or one artisan/tool proficiency related to
engineering, mining, weapons, armour, or voidcraft.
Grudge Memory: Once per long rest, when a creature 
damages you or an ally within 30 ft, mark that
creature as the subject of a grudge. The first time you hit 
that creature before the end of the encounter,
add your proficiency bonus to the damage.
Stubborn Kin: You have advantage on saving throws 
against being frightened.

species.name: Aeldari / Eldar
species.description:
3.6 Aeldari / Eldar
Aeldari are ancient xenos whose reflexes, senses, and 
psychic presence far exceed human norms. Player
Aeldari should represent rare outcasts, rangers, corsair-
adjacent wanderers, or warlocks operating
under a specific hidden purpose.
Ability Scores: +2 Dexterity, +1 Intelligence or Wisdom.
Size: Medium.
Speed: 35 ft.
Available Classes: Aeldari Outcast, Aeldari Warlock.
3.6.1 Aeldari Traits
Darkvision: You have darkvision to a range of 90 ft (see 
the rules at the start of this chapter).
Inhuman Grace: Gain proficiency in Acrobatics or 
Stealth.
Keen Senses: Gain proficiency in Perception. If you 
already have Perception proficiency, add +1 to
Perception checks instead.
Battle Trance: You may move through the space of 
allied creatures without treating it as difficult
terrain. Once per short rest, when you move at least 10 ft 
before making a weapon attack, add +1d4 to
the attack roll.
Ancient Mind: You have advantage on saving throws 
against being charmed or frightened by non-psychic 
effects.
Xenos Distrust: You have disadvantage on Persuasion 
checks with most Imperial authorities unless
disguised, vouched for, or operating under an established 
truce.

Raised in devotion, ritual, sacrifice, and Imperial worship.
Allowed Species: Human, rare Ratling.
Skill Proficiency: Religion and either Persuasion or 
Intimidation.
Litany of Resolve: Once per long rest, you can give 
yourself or one ally within 30 ft. advantage on a Wisdom

heretic, daemon, mutant, witch, traitor, or xenos with
a weapon attack or class feature, you deal an additional 
1d4 + 1 radiant damage.
This damage represents zeal, ritual fury, and trained 
hatred rather than true divine magic.

featureCatalogue.description:
A Psyker has a score called Warp Pressure.
Warp Pressure starts at 0.
Whenever you use a psychic power, increase your Warp 
Pressure by that power’s cost.
After resolving the power, roll a d20. If the result is equal 
to or lower than your current Warp Pressure,
Perils of the Warp triggers.

● You cast Focused Rupture.
● Focused Rupture adds +2 Warp Pressure.
● Your Warp Pressure is now 7.
● You roll a d20.
● On a 1- 7, Perils trigger.

Skill Proficiency: Choose two from Acrobatics, Insight, 
Perception, Stealth, Survival, and Technology.
Path Discipline: Once per long rest, when you fail a 
Wisdom or Intelligence saving throw, you may
reroll it. You must use the new result.
Alien Poise: You have advantage on checks to move 
silently through ruins, forests, webway structures,
wraithbone architecture, or abandoned alien sites.

presentation.summary: Raised among Aeldari ways, then sent away, exiled, self- exiled, ranger-bound, corsair-adjacent, or drawn into a dangerous path beyond normal craftworld protection.

featureCatalogue.name: Forge World benefits
featureCatalogue.description:
4.5 Forge World
Raised among manufactorums, machine temples, data-
vaults, and sacred industry.
Allowed Species: Human, Skitarii.
Skill Proficiency: Investigation and Technology.
Machine Rites: You can perform basic maintenance on 
weapons, armour, augmetics, cogitators, and
power systems.
Logic Before Fear: Once per long rest, you may gain 
advantage on a saving throw against fear, panic, or
psychic manipulation.

presentation.summary: Raised among manufactorums, machine temples, data- vaults, and sacred industry.

featureCatalogue.name: Hiveborn benefits
featureCatalogue.description:
4.1 Hiveborn
Raised in the brutal density of a hive city.
Allowed Species: Human, Ratling, rare Ogryn.
Skill Proficiency: Choose one from Deception, Insight, 
Intimidation, Sleight of Hand, or Stealth.
Crowd Rat: You ignore difficult terrain caused by 
crowds, rubble, cramped spaces, pipes, gantries, and
dense urban clutter.
Seen Worse: You have advantage on saving throws 
against fear caused by gore, violence, intimidation,
or battlefield horror.

presentation.summary: Raised in the brutal density of a hive city.

featureCatalogue.name: Militarum Regiment benefits
featureCatalogue.description:
4.7 Militarum Regiment
Formerly attached to an Imperial Guard force, auxiliary 
formation, or battlefield logistics unit.
Allowed Species: Human, Ogryn, Ratling, limited 
Skitarii.
Skill Proficiency: Choose one from Athletics or Survival, 
and gain Perception.
Squad Drill: Before initiative is rolled, choose one ally 
within 5 ft of you who can see or hear you. You
and that chosen ally each gain +1 to initiative for that 
combat. You must choose the ally before anyone
rolls initiative. If no ally is within 5 ft when initiative is 
called, this feature provides no benefit.
Field Discipline: Once per short rest, you may reroll a 
failed saving throw against Suppression.

presentation.summary: Formerly attached to an Imperial Guard force, auxiliary formation, or battlefield logistics unit.

featureCatalogue.name: Mining Hold / Guild benefits
featureCatalogue.description:
4.10 Mining Hold / Guild
Raised in a Squat/Kin hold, mining fleet, oath-band, 
salvage guild, prospecting clan, or void-industrial
enclave.
Allowed Species: Squat/Kin.
Skill Proficiency: Choose two from Athletics, 
Investigation, Survival, Technology, and Persuasion.
Oath and Ledger: You can usually identify the likely 
value, industrial purpose, or salvage use of
machinery, ore, weapons, armour, and voidship 
components.
Hold-Fast: Once per short rest, when you fail a saving 
throw against being frightened, knocked prone,
moved, or suppressed, you may reroll it. You must use 
the new result.

presentation.summary: Raised in a Squat/Kin hold, mining fleet, oath-band, salvage guild, prospecting clan, or void-industrial enclave.

featureCatalogue.name: Penal Worlder benefits
featureCatalogue.description:
4.3 Penal Worlder
A convict, survivor, conscript, or former prisoner.
Allowed Species: Human, Ogryn, Ratling.
Skill Proficiency: Survival and one of Athletics, 
Deception, or Intimidation.
Hard Time: You have advantage on saving throws 
against exhaustion caused by forced marches,
starvation, poor conditions, or sleep deprivation.
Dirty Survival: Once per long rest, when you are 
reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you
may drop to 1 hit point instead.

presentation.summary: A convict, survivor, conscript, or former prisoner.

featureCatalogue.name: Schola Progenium benefits
featureCatalogue.description:
4.6 Schola Progenium
Raised in harsh Imperial institutions to become a soldier, 
judge, officer, priest, or specialist.
Allowed Species: Human.
Skill Proficiency: Choose one from History or Religion, 
and one from Intimidation or Persuasion.
Drilled Obedience: You have advantage on saving 
throws against fear while following a direct order,
holding formation, or protecting an Imperial objective.
Imperial Education: You can identify major Imperial 
organisations, ranks, symbols, rites, and
procedures.

presentation.summary: Raised in harsh Imperial institutions to become a soldier, judge, officer, priest, or specialist.

featureCatalogue.name: Shrine Worlder benefits
featureCatalogue.description:
4.2 Shrine Worlder
Raised in devotion, ritual, sacrifice, and Imperial worship.
Allowed Species: Human, rare Ratling.
Skill Proficiency: Religion and either Persuasion or 
Intimidation.
Litany of Resolve: Once per long rest, you can give 
yourself or one ally within 30 ft. advantage on a Wisdom 
saving throw.
Sacred Hatred: Once per turn, when you damage a 
heretic, daemon, mutant, witch, traitor, or xenos with
a weapon attack or class feature, you deal an additional 
1d4 + 1 radiant damage.
This damage represents zeal, ritual fury, and trained 
hatred rather than true divine magic.

presentation.summary: Raised in devotion, ritual, sacrifice, and Imperial worship.

featureCatalogue.name: Underhive benefits
featureCatalogue.description:
4.8 Underhive
Raised below the proper world, among gangs, sump-rats, 
chem dens, scavvers, and forgotten habs.
Allowed Species: Human, Ratling.
Skill Proficiency: Choose two from Deception, 
Intimidation, Sleight of Hand, Stealth, and Survival.
Black-Market Instinct: You know how to locate illegal 
goods, smugglers, fences, and information
brokers in hive settlements.
Never Fight Fair: Once per short rest, when you hit a 
creature that has not acted yet in combat, deal
additional damage equal to your proficiency bonus.

presentation.summary: Raised below the proper world, among gangs, sump-rats, chem dens, scavvers, and forgotten habs.

featureCatalogue.name: Voidborn benefits
featureCatalogue.description:
4.4 Voidborn
Born aboard a voidship, orbital station, warship, pilgrim 
vessel, or ancient wreck.
Allowed Species: Human, Ratling, rare Ogryn.
Skill Proficiency: Choose one from Acrobatics, 
Perception, Investigation, or Technology.
Void Legs: You have advantage on checks and saving 
throws to avoid being knocked prone or moved
against your will.
Shipwise: You are proficient with basic voidship 
procedures, airlocks, auspex consoles, pressure doors,
and shipboard emergency systems.

presentation.summary: Born aboard a voidship, orbital station, warship, pilgrim vessel, or ancient wreck.

featureCatalogue.description: Fixed ability adjustments and speed from species entry.

featureCatalogue.name: Aeldari / Eldar traits
featureCatalogue.description:
3.6 Aeldari / Eldar
Aeldari are ancient xenos whose reflexes, senses, and 
psychic presence far exceed human norms. Player
Aeldari should represent rare outcasts, rangers, corsair-
adjacent wanderers, or warlocks operating
under a specific hidden purpose.
Ability Scores: +2 Dexterity, +1 Intelligence or Wisdom.
Size: Medium.
Speed: 35 ft.
Available Classes: Aeldari Outcast, Aeldari Warlock.
3.6.1 Aeldari Traits
Darkvision: You have darkvision to a range of 90 ft (see 
the rules at the start of this chapter).
Inhuman Grace: Gain proficiency in Acrobatics or 
Stealth.
Keen Senses: Gain proficiency in Perception. If you 
already have Perception proficiency, add +1 to
Perception checks instead.
Battle Trance: You may move through the space of 
allied creatures without treating it as difficult
terrain. Once per short rest, when you move at least 10 ft 
before making a weapon attack, add +1d4 to
the attack roll.
Ancient Mind: You have advantage on saving throws 
against being charmed or frightened by non-psychic 
effects.
Xenos Distrust: You have disadvantage on Persuasion 
checks with most Imperial authorities unless
disguised, vouched for, or operating under an established 
truce.

presentation.summary: Aeldari are ancient xenos whose reflexes, senses, and psychic presence far exceed human norms. Player Aeldari should represent rare outcasts, rangers, corsair- adjacent wanderers, or warlocks operating under a specific hidden purpose.

featureCatalogue.name: Human fixed baseline
featureCatalogue.description: Fixed ability adjustments and speed from species entry.

presentation.summary: Fixed ability adjustments and speed from species entry.

featureCatalogue.name: Human traits
featureCatalogue.description:
3.1 Human
Humans are the baseline of the Imperium: adaptable, 
ambitious, fragile, and dangerously determined.
Ability Scores: +2 to one ability score and +1 to 
another.
Size: Medium.
Speed: 30 ft.
Available Classes: Veteran, Zealot, Psyker, Arbites 
Enforcer, Hive Scum.
3.1.1 Human Traits
Imperial Adaptability: Gain proficiency in one skill of 
your choice.
Broad Training: Gain one additional weapon, tool, or 
language proficiency.
Faith, Fear, or Discipline: Once per long rest, when you 
fail a saving throw, you may reroll it. You must
use the new result.

presentation.summary: Humans are the baseline of the Imperium: adaptable, ambitious, fragile, and dangerously determined.

featureCatalogue.description: Fixed ability adjustments and speed from species entry.

presentation.summary: Fixed ability adjustments and speed from species entry.

featureCatalogue.name: Squat / Kin traits
featureCatalogue.description:
3.5 Squat / Kin
Squats, often known as Kin in modern Imperial records, 
are hardy void-adapted abhumans associated
with holds, guilds, oath-bands, mining fleets, mercenary 
contracts, and ancient grudges. They are
shorter than humans but dense, resilient, technically 
minded, and extremely difficult to intimidate.
Ability Scores: +2 Constitution, +1 Intelligence or 
Wisdom.
Size: Medium, but your height is usually between 4 and 5 
ft.
Speed: 25 ft.
Available Classes: Kin Armsman, Hernkyn Prospector.
3.5.1 Squat / Kin Traits
Darkvision: You have darkvision to a range of 60 ft (see 
the rules at the start of this chapter).
Dense Build: You have advantage on saving throws 
against being shoved, knocked prone, or moved
against your will.
Void-Hardened: You have advantage on saving throws 
against exhaustion caused by poor atmosphere,
bad rations, forced marches, cramped voidship 
conditions, mining hazards, or environmental hardship.
Guild-Craft: Gain proficiency in Technology, 
Investigation, or one artisan/tool proficiency related to
engineering, mining, weapons, armour, or voidcraft.
Grudge Memory: Once per long rest, when a creature 
damages you or an ally within 30 ft, mark that
creature as the subject of a grudge. The first time you hit 
that creature before the end of the encounter,
add your proficiency bonus to the damage.
Stubborn Kin: You have advantage on saving throws 
against being frightened.

presentation.summary: Squats, often known as Kin in modern Imperial records, are hardy void-adapted abhumans associated with holds, guilds, oath-bands, mining fleets, mercenary contracts, and ancient grudges. They are shorter than humans but dense, resilient, technically minded, and extremely difficult to intimidate.

featureCatalogue.description: Fixed ability adjustments and speed from species entry.

featureCatalogue.name: Ogryn Abhuman traits
featureCatalogue.description:
3.2 Ogryn Abhuman
Ogryns are massive abhumans used by the Imperium as 
shock troops, bodyguards, line-breakers, and
living siege weapons. They are loyal and terrifyingly 
durable, but they are not subtle and struggle with
equipment designed for normal human frames.
Ability Scores: +2 Strength, +1 Constitution.
Size: Medium, but you count as one size larger for 
carrying, lifting, pushing, dragging, grappling, and
shoving.
Speed: 30 ft.
Available Classes: Ogryn Skullbreaker only.
3.2.1 Ogryn Traits
Massive Build: Your maximum hit points increase by 3 
per character level. You also count as one size
larger for carrying, lifting, pushing, dragging, grappling, 
and shoving.
Thick Skull: You have advantage on saving throws 
against being frightened.
Brute Strength: Your unarmed strikes deal 1d6 + your 
Strength modifier bludgeoning damage.
Too Big for Standard Kit: You cannot use most 
standard armour, delicate weapons, compact firearms,
or subtle tools unless they have been modified for Ogryn 
use.
Simple Solutions: You are not automatically stupid, but 
you struggle with delicate logic, subtle
interfaces, encrypted systems, and advanced technology. 
You have disadvantage on Intelligence checks
involving advanced technology, forbidden lore, cogitators, 
security systems, encrypted data, or complex
machinery unless you are proficient in a relevant skill or 
tool. However, once per short rest, when a
problem could plausibly be solved through brute force, 
intimidation, endurance, or direct action, you
may add your proficiency bonus to the check even if you 
would not normally be proficient.

presentation.summary: Ogryns are massive abhumans used by the Imperium as shock troops, bodyguards, line-breakers, and living siege weapons. They are loyal and terrifyingly durable, but they are not subtle and struggle with equipment designed for normal human frames.

featureCatalogue.name: Ratling Abhuman traits
featureCatalogue.description:
3.3 Ratling Abhuman
Ratlings are small abhumans known for stealth, 
marksmanship, scavenging, cooking, black-market
dealings, and improbable survival.
Ability Scores: +2 Dexterity, +1 Wisdom.
Size: Small.
Speed: 25 ft.
Available Classes: Ratling Sharpshooter, Veteran, Hive 
Scum.
3.3.1 Ratling Traits
Darkvision: You have darkvision to a range of 60 ft (see 
the rules at the start of this chapter).
Small Target: When you have light cover, you may treat 
it as heavy cover.
Sniper’s Eye: You ignore disadvantage from attacking at 
long range with weapons that have the
Accurate property.
Naturally Sneaky: You gain proficiency in Stealth.
Lucky Shot: Once per short rest, when you miss with a 
ranged weapon attack, you may reroll the
attack.
Bad in a Straight Fight: You have disadvantage on 
Strength checks made to shove or grapple creatures
larger than you.

presentation.summary: Ratlings are small abhumans known for stealth, marksmanship, scavenging, cooking, black-market dealings, and improbable survival.

featureCatalogue.name: Skitarii Augmented Human traits
featureCatalogue.description:
3.4 Skitarii Augmented Human
Skitarii are cybernetically enhanced soldiers of the 
Adeptus Mechanicus. They are machine-disciplined,
sensor-linked, and doctrinally conditioned beyond normal 
human limits.
Ability Scores: +2 Dexterity or Intelligence, +1 
Constitution.
Size: Medium.
Speed: 30 ft.
Available Classes: Skitarii Veteran.
3.4.1 Skitarii Traits
Augmetic Body: You have resistance to poison damage 
and advantage on saving throws against
disease.
Machine Discipline: You have advantage on saving 
throws against being charmed.
Noospheric Focus: Gain proficiency in Investigation, 
Perception, or Technology.
Integrated Auspex: Once per short rest, as a bonus 
action, choose one creature within 60 ft that you
can see. Your next attack against that creature before 
the end of your turn gains +1d4 to hit.
Cybernetic Maintenance: During a short rest, if you or 
an ally has tinker’s tools or Mechanicus tools,
you may regain additional hit points equal to your 
proficiency bonus.
No Psychic Potential: You cannot choose the Psyker 
class or any trait that grants psychic powers.

presentation.summary: Skitarii are cybernetically enhanced soldiers of the Adeptus Mechanicus. They are machine-disciplined, sensor-linked, and doctrinally conditioned beyond normal human limits.
